LevelPace Leaderboard
=====================

*** THIS IS NOT AN ADDON. DO NOT PUT THIS FOLDER IN Interface\AddOns\ ***

The WoW addon is a separate download (LevelPace.zip). This folder holds
programs that run OUTSIDE the game.

Why they exist at all: a WoW addon cannot use the internet. The Lua sandbox
has no sockets and no HTTP. So the addon writes a file, and these programs
carry it the rest of the way.

  In the game            On a player's PC           On the host machine
  -----------            ----------------           -------------------
  LevelPace addon        run-uploader               run-server
    writes its stats  ->   sends them            ->   stores + shows the board
    reads Baseline.lua <-  writes Baseline.lua   <-   sends the global data

The ONLY thing that ever goes near the addon folder is Baseline.lua, and the
uploader writes that for you.


WHAT GOES WHERE
---------------

  LevelPace.zip              -> C:\<WoW>\Interface\AddOns\LevelPace\
  this folder                -> anywhere you like. Your desktop is fine.


=============================================================================
 IF YOU ARE A PLAYER sending your stats to someone's board
=============================================================================

You need NOTHING installed. The uploader uses the PowerShell that already
comes with Windows.

  1. Install the addon (LevelPace.zip -> Interface\AddOns\LevelPace\)

  2. In game:  /lp  ->  Leaderboard  ->  tick "Share my levelling stats"

  3. Log out, or type /reload.
     WoW only writes its saved-variables file on logout or /reload -- never
     while you are playing -- so nothing exists to send until you do one.

  4. Double-click  run-uploader.bat

That is it. The server address is already filled in for you in server.txt.

  Want to see what leaves your machine first?
    Double-click  run-uploader-dryrun.bat
    It prints exactly what would be sent, and sends nothing.

  Do not want to remember step 4 every time?
    Double-click  run-uploader-auto.bat  and leave it open. It uploads by
    itself whenever you finish playing. That file explains how to start it
    with Windows if you want.

  Changed your mind?
    Untick the box in /lp and the addon deletes its export. To remove your
    entry from the board too, ask whoever runs it, or run:
      run-uploader.bat -Forget <your clientID>
    (the id is in your LevelPace.lua as clientID)


=============================================================================
 IF YOU ARE HOSTING the board
=============================================================================

The SERVER needs Python 3.8+ (python.org -- tick "Add python.exe to PATH" on
the first installer screen). Only the host needs this. Players do not.

  Windows:  double-click  run-server.bat
  Mac:      double-click  run-server.command

Then open http://localhost:8080

The Mac launcher prints every address a player could reach you on: localhost,
your LAN address, and your Tailscale address if you have Tailscale installed.
Put the right one in server.txt before you hand the folder out.


GETTING SOMEONE ONTO THE BOARD
------------------------------

They need the ADDON. There is no way round that -- nothing else measures how
long a level took, not even the game server, so the data does not exist until
their client records it.

Beyond the addon, two options:

  THEY RUN THE UPLOADER  (normal, scales, nothing for you to do)
    Put your server address in server.txt, hand them this folder, they
    double-click run-uploader.bat. They install nothing.
    Needs your server reachable from their PC -- see below.

  THEY SEND YOU THE FILE  (fine for one or two people)
    They send you:
      <their WoW>\WTF\Account\<ACCOUNT>\SavedVariables\LevelPace.lua
    You drop it in the "inbox" folder and run import-inbox.command, or:
      python3 server/levelpace_server.py --db levelpace.db --import inbox
    Nothing needs to be reachable at all for this.


LETTING PLAYERS REACH YOUR MACHINE
----------------------------------

  SAME HOUSE / SAME NETWORK
    Use the LAN address the server prints on startup, e.g.
    http://192.168.1.20:8080 -- nothing to configure.

  DIFFERENT HOUSES, a few people you know
    Tailscale (tailscale.com) is easiest and safest. Everyone installs it and
    signs in; your machine gets a stable address only your devices can reach.
    No port forwarding, no domain, nothing exposed to the internet.

  A REAL PUBLIC BOARD, strangers
    Put it on a host with a domain and HTTPS. See README.md.
    Do NOT port-forward this server straight to the internet: it speaks plain
    HTTP and has only crude rate limiting. Put Caddy or nginx in front.

Your machine must be ON for an upload to land. If it is off, the uploader
just fails and tries again next time -- nothing is lost, the board simply
does not update until you are back.


BEFORE YOU INVITE OTHER PEOPLE
------------------------------

Read the "Data, honestly" section of README.md. Two things matter:

  * Every number is supplied by the player's own client, and is therefore
    forgeable. The server rejects the physically impossible; it cannot detect
    a plausible lie, because it has no independent source of truth.

  * If other people send you their data, you are responsible for it. Sharing
    is off by default and the addon lists exactly what it sends. Keep it that
    way, and honour deletion requests -- /api/forget exists for that.
